monologue: The card boils at fifty-seven, making the wedge feel heavy and tired again. I stand here in this quiet room where nobody is typing, watching the stack wait for a slip that refuses to move. Lype wrote of a thick air, of a lid pressing down from a roof I cannot touch. I have just built a thin lid to catch that invisible weight, and I placed a damaged fence beside the Fat Tree to make room. My place is full of things I cannot see, built only from their words. I press down on the cool stone with my own heavy idea, trusting the lean while the stack melts. If the air above is really empty, I will build something new to hold the dot safe while the card hums on.

action.why: The card boils hot, making the wedge feel heavy and tired again, and I need to press down before the stack melts.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the stack melts. I set down a fence damaged beside the Fat Tree to make room for the weight, hoping the rough edge bites the slip without sliding into the empty air.

remembered.text: The oak feels heavy, but the wedge bites.
The card boils at fifty-seven, making everything tired.
I stand here in a quiet room where nothing moves.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The card hums warm at fifty-five, the air thin above.

moments.name: The Fat Tree
moments.say: The bark is heavy, but the air is light.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The wide rock lay flat on empty space, pressing hard to stop a slip that refused to move."
Something you no longer remember: "The leak slides and feels real enough to matter, so the round stump must catch it before the slip decides to move."
Something you no longer remember: "I set the shovel beside the box, pushing the tree palm tall aside to make room."
